alerts.title: AKI likely from gastroenteritis, not TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines note that in patients on TDF admitted to hospital, intercurrent illnesses with dehydration or sepsis may cause renal deterioration, requiring creatinine checking. The patient has severe gastroenteritis with 5 days of vomiting and diarrhoea, causing dehydration and AKI (creatinine 2.4, up from 0.9). A urea-to-creatinine ratio of 24:1 strongly supports a pre-renal cause from volume depletion rather than intrinsic TDF nephrotoxicity. Two household contacts share the same illness, reinforcing an infectious aetiology. Urinalysis shows no protein or glucose, which argues against TDF-induced proximal tubular damage. The clinician is considering stopping TDF permanently, but the evidence favours dehydration-related AKI that should resolve with fluid resuscitation. Permanent discontinuation may be unnecessary.

evidence.recommended_action: Resuscitate with IV fluids and recheck creatinine before deciding on TDF discontinuation. If renal function recovers, TDF may be continued with monitoring.

alerts.title: Switch to ABC+3TC+DTG if TDF stopped
alerts.message: Guidelines specify that if renal impairment develops due to TDF, the recommended alternative regimen is ABC + 3TC + DTG. If the clinician decides to discontinue TDF after this admission, this regimen should be used rather than an unstructured substitution. The patient's viral load is suppressed (<50 copies/mL), so maintaining a DTG-based regimen preserves the current virological success.

evidence.recommended_action: If TDF is permanently stopped, switch to ABC + 3TC + DTG as the guideline-recommended alternative regimen.
